findings.message: No beat reaches 6/10 in the first 10% of the experience (best is 3). Players decide early whether to keep going.
findings.suggestion: Open with a short, legible high-interest moment (a promise of the core fantasy, a striking reveal, or a quick win), then dip to teach.

findings.message: 0.0-8.0: intensity stays within ±0.5 around 2.9 for 8.0 units (low and flat: boredom and quit risk).
findings.suggestion: Insert a contrast beat: a twist on the current mechanic, a new threat, a reveal, a reward, or a deliberate rest that sets up the next rise.

findings.message: The strongest moment (10, The drowned keeper tears through the pump hall; flee upstairs) happens at 30% of the experience; later beats never top it.
findings.suggestion: Move or build a climax into the last 30%, or reduce the early peak so the ending is the highest point.

findings.message: 11.3-20.0: intensity stays at or above 8 for 8.7 units (22% of the run).
findings.suggestion: Break the plateau into two peaks with a short release between them, or vary the kind of intensity (spatial, cognitive, emotional).

findings.message: Peaks after the hook don't rise (trend -6.6 points across the run).
findings.suggestion: Make each major peak a little stronger or more complex than the last: sawtooth upward, resetting lower after each release.

findings.message: 13.0-20.0: intensity stays within ±0.5 around 8.1 for 7.0 units (high and flat: numbness and fatigue risk).
findings.suggestion: Insert a contrast beat: a twist on the current mechanic, a new threat, a reveal, a reward, or a deliberate rest that sets up the next rise.

findings.message: Peak at 20.0 (8, Return through the same pursuit corridor) is not followed by a drop of 2.5+ within 4.8 units.
findings.suggestion: After a peak, give a release beat (safe room, loot, story, shop, short traversal) so the next peak lands harder.

findings.message: 20.1-30.1: intensity stays within ±0.5 around 7.1 for 10.0 units (high and flat: numbness and fatigue risk).
findings.suggestion: Insert a contrast beat: a twist on the current mechanic, a new threat, a reveal, a reward, or a deliberate rest that sets up the next rise.
